combat_history.event: Pinaka saw use during the Kargil conflict in its early form.
combat_history.significance: Early combat employment of the indigenous system.

combat_history.event: Armenia signed deals to import Pinaka systems.
combat_history.significance: Established Pinaka as an Indian artillery export.

modernization.description: Guidance kits and longer-range rockets; large Army orders.
modernization.impact: Turns area rocket fire into precision long-range fires.

vulnerabilities.description: Large signature on firing; vulnerable if static.
The baseline rocket is an area weapon with dispersion.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Massed area and precision rocket fire supporting Indian Army operations, mainly on the western and northern fronts.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Scaling up; guided variants entering service.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: China's PHL-191 reaches far greater ranges with larger rockets and tactical missiles; the Pinaka is shorter-ranged but indigenous and mass-producible.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: India and China's rocket artillery compared.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: HIMARS fires fewer but longer-range precision rockets/missiles; the Pinaka emphasises salvo mass with growing precision.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Mass vs precision in rocket artillery.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: India operates the heavier Russian Smerch; the Pinaka is the indigenous complement.

doctrine.role: Indigenous multiple rocket launcher for massed area and precision long-range fires.
doctrine.employment: Rapid 12-rocket salvos to saturate targets; guided variants for precision shoot-and-scoot.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Sovereign, mass-producible rocket fires complementing tube artillery.
doctrine.threat_context: Long-range fires on India's western and northern fronts; a growing export.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against China's PHL-191, the US HIMARS and Russia's Smerch.
